title: B2+ · L48 — Sustainability vocabulary
description: Vocabulario de sostenibilidad: carbon footprint, net-zero, circular economy, ESG, greenwashing.

questions.prompt: En un all-hands, el CEO menciona reducir el 'carbon footprint' de la empresa.
questions.question: 'Carbon footprint' means:
options: The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by an entity or activity.
questions.explanation: Carbon footprint = huella de carbono, total de emisiones GEI (medido en CO2 equivalente) de persona, empresa, producto o pais. Metrica base del climate discourse. Se 'measures', 'reduces', 'offsets'.
examples: Our biggest carbon footprint comes from business travel and data centers.
Flying less is the single easiest way to cut a personal footprint. → advice concreto

questions.prompt: Reporte anual dice: 'We aim to be net-zero by 2040.'
questions.question: 'Net-zero' means:
options: Balancing emissions produced with emissions removed.
questions.explanation: Net-zero = emisiones netas cero: se emite X pero se remueve/compensa X. NO es cero emisiones absolutas ('absolute zero'). Concepto clave post-Acuerdo de Paris. Critica valida: net-zero puede depender demasiado de offsets dudosos.
examples: Net-zero by 2050 is the global consensus target.
Absolute zero is harder than net-zero — no offsets, just no emissions. → matiz importante

questions.statement: The 'circular economy' aims to eliminate waste by reusing, repairing, and recycling materials continuously.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Circular economy = modelo que disena OUT el residuo: los materiales se reutilizan, reparan, reciclan en bucle. Opuesto al modelo lineal ('take-make-waste'). Framework popularizado por Ellen MacArthur Foundation.
examples: A circular economy treats waste as a design flaw.
Patagonia's repair program is textbook circular economy. → ejemplo concreto

questions.prompt: Investor pregunta por los 'ESG metrics' del fondo.
questions.question: 'ESG' stands for:
questions.explanation: ESG = Environmental, Social, Governance. Framework para evaluar sostenibilidad y etica de una empresa. Usado por investors para screening. Discutido en 2024+: acusado de greenwashing pero sigue siendo lingua franca del sustainable finance.
examples: Our ESG rating improved after the diversity reforms.
ESG has become politicized in the US but is standard in the EU. → matiz geopolitico

questions.text: The company claims to be sustainable, but honestly, most of it looks like greenwashing to me.
questions.explanation: Discurso critico y natural. 'Greenwashing' (marketing enganoso sobre sostenibilidad) — palabra clave del climate discourse. Discourse marker 'honestly' y hedge 'to me' suavizan la acusacion. En hablado 'looks like' se contrae en 'looks-like' con linking suave.
examples: Real sustainability is measured, not marketed.
Greenwashing hurts the credibility of the whole movement. → argumento comun

questions.prompt: Empresa anuncia 'carbon offsets' para compensar emisiones de vuelos.
questions.question: A 'carbon offset' is:
options: A credit representing emissions reduced elsewhere to compensate your own.
questions.explanation: Carbon offset = credito que representa emisiones reducidas/removidas en otro lugar (reforestacion, energia renovable, captura) para compensar las tuyas. Herramienta controvertida: muchos offsets son de baja calidad o no adicionales. Termino omnipresente en corporate sustainability.
examples: We buy verified offsets for every flight we can't avoid.
Not all offsets are equal — some are pure paper. → escepticismo saludable

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de sostenibilidad con su definicion:

pairs.right: Diversidad de especies en un ecosistema

questions.explanation: Vocabulario nucleo climate/sustainability. 'Renewable' se usa como adjetivo Y como nombre ('the renewables sector'). 'Biodiversity loss' es la segunda gran crisis ambiental despues del climate change, muchas veces subestimada.
examples: Renewables now generate over 40% of the EU's electricity.
Biodiversity loss is the silent twin of climate change. → framing sofisticado

questions.target: Honestly, the hardest part of decarbonizing our supply chain isn't the tech — it's getting suppliers to actually measure and report their scope-three emissions.
questions.explanation: Discurso corporate sustainability senior. 'Decarbonizing' (verbo tecnico), 'supply chain' (colocacion), 'scope-three emissions' (categoria GHG protocol: emisiones indirectas de la cadena de valor — las mas dificiles). Argumento maduro: el problema es data/coordinacion, no tecnologia.
examples: Scope three is 80% of our footprint and 100% of the headache.
Suppliers won't measure what customers don't demand. → causa-efecto

questions.prompt: Report climate: 'We must ___ from fossil fuels within this decade.'
questions.question: Complete:
questions.explanation: 'Transition from/away from' es el verbo estandar del climate discourse. 'Energy transition' es un termino tecnico (paso de fosiles a renovables). 'Escape' es dramatico y no aplica. 'Just transition' anade la dimension social: proteger a trabajadores del cambio.
examples: The energy transition needs to be fast AND just.
We can't transition off fossil fuels without a plan for coal towns. → matiz social

questions.statement: 'Climate change' and 'global warming' mean exactly the same thing.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Relacionados pero distintos. 'Global warming' = tendencia al alza de temperaturas medias. 'Climate change' = conjunto mas amplio de cambios (temperatura, precipitacion, eventos extremos, oceanos). Cientificos prefieren 'climate change' o 'climate crisis' — captura mejor el problema.
examples: Global warming causes climate change, but climate change is broader.
The term 'climate crisis' better conveys the urgency. → uso preferido actual

questions.prompt: En un panel, alguien dice 'we need to phase out coal'.
questions.question: 'Phase out' means:
questions.explanation: Phase out = eliminar gradualmente segun un plan por fases. Opuesto: 'phase in' (introducir gradualmente). Verbo clave en policy climate: 'phase out coal by 2030'. Distinto de 'ban' (prohibir inmediatamente) o 'shut down' (cierre puntual).
examples: The UK phased out coal power in just over a decade.
Phase-out plans without dates are just wishful thinking. → critique escepticista

questions.text: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and more intense, and the science on the cause is unambiguous.
questions.explanation: Discurso IPCC-style, muy comun en news broadcasting. 'Extreme weather events', 'more frequent and more intense' (paralelismo), 'the science is unambiguous' (frase de assertion cientifica). Nota el ritmo: hay tres pausas naturales entre clausulas coordinadas.
examples: The link between warming and extreme weather is now unambiguous.
Adaptation is no longer optional — it's baseline planning. → policy shift

questions.prompt: Startup pitch: 'We're building tech to enable ___ agriculture.'
questions.question: Complete with the buzzword of modern farming sustainability:
questions.explanation: 'Regenerative' agriculture = mas alla de sustainable: activamente restaura suelo, biodiversidad, agua. Vocabulario moderno (post-2018). Se contrapone a 'industrial' (extractivo). En 2024+ es palabra clave de food-tech y climate VC.
examples: Regenerative farming can turn soil into a carbon sink.
Sustainable is doing less harm; regenerative is doing more good. → definicion elegante

questions.statement: 'Carbon-neutral' and 'net-zero' are often used interchangeably but have technical differences.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. En marketing se usan como sinonimos pero: 'carbon-neutral' historicamente cubre solo CO2 y depende mas de offsets. 'Net-zero' es mas amplio (todos los GEI) y suele exigir reduccion real antes de compensar. Un experto ESG notara la diferencia.
examples: Marketing says 'carbon-neutral'; the auditor asks 'net-zero on scope one, two, and three?'
Real net-zero requires actual reductions, not just offsets. → punto tecnico

questions.target: Look, we can debate offsets and ESG scores all day, but the truth is: we need absolute emissions cuts, and we need them this decade — not by 2050.
questions.explanation: Discurso climate activist/leader maduro. 'Look' (discourse marker de assertion), contraste 'debate all day vs need cuts', urgencia temporal 'this decade — not 2050'. Argumento retorico clave: distinguir talk de action. Muy comun en TED talks y climate summits.
examples: Targets without action are corporate poetry.
The 2020s are the decisive decade — everything else is stalling. → framing IPCC
